title: Self-RAG: Learning to Retrieve, Generate, and Critique through Self-Reflection
layout_note: Baseline RAG in a narrower left panel and 'Ours' Self-RAG in a wider right panel, split by a solid grey vertical rule; a dotted horizontal rule cuts off a short bottom strip that repeats the comparison on a second prompt, where Self-RAG skips retrieval. Each panel walks one worked example through numbered steps.
grouping: No boxes around the panels: the vertical rule, the dotted rule and the bold panel titles do the grouping. Inside each panel, 'Step N:' headings (the step number in blue, the description in black bold) separate the stages; in the Self-RAG panel, Step 2 is three parallel columns (Prompt + 1, Prompt + 2, Prompt + 3), one per retrieved passage. Text colour carries judgement: generated text is green, wrong or unsupported text is red and underlined, and the reflection-token chips form one colour family (green, salmon, orange).
shapes_depth: Flat. Prompts and retrieved passages sit in light-grey filled rounded rectangles with no outline; passages are set in a grey slab-serif typewriter face, everything else in sans-serif. Passages are referenced by black discs with white numerals that reappear wherever the passage is used. Reflection tokens are small square-cornered chips with a dark blue outline and a solid fill; Retrieve and No Retrieval are white chips with a brown or dark-grey outline and matching text. Critiques of the baseline are white speech-bubble callouts with grey outlines pointing at the faulty words. Short solid grey arrows mark generation, curved dashed light-grey arrows route retrieval, and one blue dashed curved arrow feeds the selected segment back to the LM. Small black line icons stand for the LM (a node-and-edge network), the retriever (a magnifier) and the critique step (a gauge); '>' glyphs rank the candidate segments.
proposed_highlight: The method panel is wider than the baseline's, and its title gives the method's name in red after a black 'Ours:'. The method's own vocabulary, the reflection tokens, is the only saturated fill in the figure: chips labelled Relevant, Irrelevant, Supported and Partially sit beside each generated segment, and Step 3 ranks the segments as rows of bare chips joined by '>' glyphs, the winner wrapped in a blue rounded outline.
lesson: Running the baseline and the method on the same worked example in adjacent panels, with errors set as red underlined text and the method's judgements as coloured chips beside each segment, lets a reader compare the outcomes without reading every sentence.
notes: elements 'other' = the black numbered discs used as passage references and citation marks in the final output, and the reflection-token chips. The network and gauge icons and most numbered discs are embedded images recorded by refs crop, so they are left out of the palette. Venue ICLR as recorded (venue_source semantic-scholar); year = arXiv preprint year (2310.11511).

measured.source: computed: paperfig kb measure (non-white pixels of a <= 800 px thumbnail, white = min(R,G,B) >= 245, minus the embedded images recorded by `refs crop` (images_px; their share is photo_share, null without a record); chromatic (RGB spread > 20) and neutral pixels clustered separately by PIL median-cut + k-means (k=8 / 3); clusters within dE00 4 merged; kept if >= 0.02 of chromatic pixels / neutral ones if >= 0.03 of all non-white pixels; share = fraction of the non-photo non-white pixels)

core.what: baseline RAG in a narrower left panel and Self-RAG ('Ours') in a wider right panel, split by a vertical rule, both run on the same prompt, with a bottom strip repeating the comparison on a prompt that needs no retrieval

relations.form: two side-by-side panels on the same prompt separated by a solid vertical rule, ours on the right and wider; a dotted horizontal rule cuts off a second, one-line comparison below
within each panel numbered 'Step N:' headings run top to bottom (retrieve, generate, critique)
a magnifying-glass retriever beside the flow returns passages drawn as data: grey rounded boxes with real text, numbered by black circled digits that are reused as tokens later
Self-RAG Step 2 draws three parallel columns 'Prompt + 1/2/3', each with its own LM glyph, generated segment and reflection-token chips
Step 3 ranks the three segments in one row with large '>' signs (1 > 3 > 2), the winner circled in blue and fed back to the LM by a blue dashed arrow

channels.colour: green text = supported generation and red underlined text = contradicted or irrelevant content; reflection-token chips are filled green (Relevant/Supported), red (Irrelevant), orange (Partially) or outlined brown (Retrieve); red is also used for the 'Ours: Self-RAG' title, so red carries both 'wrong' and 'ours'; blue marks 'Step N' labels
channels.shape: grey rounded chips = prompts and passages; small rectangular coloured chips = reflection tokens; a network glyph = the LM; a magnifier = the retriever; black circled digits = passage ids
channels.line: grey dashed curves = passages routed from the retriever to prompts; solid grey short arrows = generation; a blue dashed arrow = the selected segment fed back
channels.frame: panels are delimited by rules, not boxes; a blue rounded outline marks the selected segment in Step 3

quality.strengths: Both methods run on the same real prompt with real passages and generations, so the difference is shown as data, not described; reflection tokens appear as coloured chips exactly where they are emitted; the 1 > 3 > 2 ranking makes the critique step visible as an ordering; the bottom strip shows the no-retrieval case in one line per method.
quality.weaknesses: The two panels are not drawn with the same layout, so the steps do not align across the rule for a direct comparison; red means both 'erroneous' and 'ours' (title); long grey dashed curves from the retriever through the 1-2-3 digits to the three prompts cross the right panel; Step 3 is dense with small chips and text.

insights.structure: A narrower baseline RAG panel at left and a wider 'Ours' Self-RAG panel at right, split by a solid grey vertical rule, with a dotted horizontal rule cutting off a bottom strip that repeats both on a second prompt where Self-RAG skips retrieval.
insights.data: Everything is one worked example in real text: grey prompt chips, retrieved passages in grey rounded boxes numbered by black circled digits, generations in green, errors in red underline, and reflection tokens (Retrieve, Relevant, Irrelevant, Supported, Partially, No Retrieval) as small coloured chips.
insights.emphasis: The Self-RAG title is in red, its panel is wider, and the coloured reflection chips plus the ranking '1 > 3 > 2' in Step 3 show the critique that the baseline lacks.
insights.flow: Top to bottom by blue-numbered 'Step N:' headings; inside steps, dashed grey curved arrows fan from the retriever magnifier to three parallel 'Prompt + k' columns, and a blue dashed arrow loops the chosen segment back to the LM for the next round.
insights.avoid: The panels are dense with small type, callout bubbles overlap the baseline's output text, and a stray red '4' badge sits in the final output; keep fewer words per step and keep callouts clear of the text.

arrangement.units: two unboxed side-by-side panels separated by rules, each with 'Step N' text sections; a bottom strip repeats both
arrangement.inputs_as: a real prompt in a grey chip at the top of each panel
arrangement.shared: the same prompt, retriever icon and LM network glyph appear in both panels
